method: Executed the exact lesson Python fence with deterministic FakeClient fixtures and ran the 7-assertion offline verifier. The verifier rejects malformed/duplicate tool envelopes before dispatch, checks fixed host allowlist denials, compares the complete published stdout, and binds MCP tools/list metadata claims to the registered official Tools source. Reviewed the 2026-07-28 MCP Tools and Security Best Practices documents. No provider or external network call.
limitations: FakeClient proposals are fixed synthetic fixtures; they do not measure whether any model follows indirect prompt injection or how tool metadata changes model behavior.
The fixed read_doc allowlist is a teaching gate. No production identity, tenant/object authorization, approval, revocation, concurrency, audit pipeline, or external side effect was tested.
Historical provider observations and the reported seven-attempt injection summary remain unreproduced because raw requests, responses, and a reproducible scorer are unavailable.
MCP protocol metadata and annotations do not prove a server implementation, runtime permission, or actual side-effect behavior.
